Irenæus excellently declaring that the Church and euery {{ls}}piritual childe thereof, iudgeth and condemneth al fal{{ls}}e Prophets and Heretikes of vvhat {{ls}}ort {{ls}}o euer, at length he concludeth vvith the{{ls}}e notable wordes: {{outside R|The Church is vnder no mans iudgement.}}{{outside L|''Iren. li. 4. c. 62''.}}''The {{ls}}piritual {{ls}}hal iudge al{{ls}}o all that make {{ls}}chi{{ls}}mes, which be cruel, not hauing the loue of God, and re{{ls}}pecting their ovvne priuate, more then the vnitie of the Church: mangle, deuide, and (as much as in them lieth) kill for {{ls}}mal causes the great and glorious body of Chri{{ls}}t, {{ls}}peaking peace, and {{ls}}eeking battaile. He {{ls}}hal iudge al{{ls}}o them that be out of the truth, that is to {{ls}}ay. out of the Church: which Church {{ls}}hal be vnder no mans iudgement. for to the Church are al things knowen, in which is perfect faith of the Father, and of al the di{{ls}}pen{{ls}}ation of Chri{{ls}}t, and firme knovvledge of the Holy Gho{{ls}}t that teacheth all truth''.

{{c|''If they vvil not be carnal {{ls}}til, they mu{{ls}}t boa{{ls}}t in God only, & not in their preachers, Which are but his mini{{ls}}ters, 10 and neede to looke vvel hovv they preach: 12 becau{{ls}}e not al preaching, though it be Catholike, is meritorious: but rather it buildeth matter to be purged by fire, vvhen it is vaine and vnfruitful (as al{{ls}}o any other like vvorkes of other Catholikes.) marie if it be heretical, de{{ls}}troying the temple of God, then it vvorketh damnation. 18 The remedie is, to humble them {{ls}}elues and referre al to God.''}}
